subject: Request: exclude downstream peering outage from uptime calculation
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: ops@nexuscloud.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: exclude downstream peering outage from uptime calculation

Hi Nexus Ops team,

We observed a partial degradation for customers in us-west on 2027-04-11 between 15:03:00 UTC and 16:37:00 UTC. Our telemetry shows elevated tail latency and a visible increase in 5xxs for requests that traversed a specific Nexus peering fabric (ASN 64512). Attached is a concise timeline (nexus_outage_timeline.csv) and a BGP dump + edge logs.

Summary:
- Window: 2027-04-11 15:03:00 UTC -> 16:37:00 UTC
- Impact: ~14% of production requests from us-west experienced >200ms p95 and a small bump in 5xxs
- Root cause (our initial triage): Nexus performed an emergency maintenance on a downstream peering node which caused partial route flaps; Redwood’s multi-path routing avoided full outage for most users but a subset was routed through the affected peer.

Per our SLA (section 4.2 third-party exclusions) we believe this qualifies for a third-party exclusion because the affected path was downstream and outside Redwood’s managed fabric. We are requesting Nexus mark that interval as excluded from uptime tally for the purposes of SLA credit calculation and to confirm whether we should apply pro-rata credit given partial degradation.

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Nexus will exclude the window above from Redwood’s uptime calculation.
2) If Nexus needs additional artifacts, we’ve included logs but can provide PCAPs and full BGP update walks on request.
3) If exclusion is not accepted, please share the specific criteria or evidence Nexus needs so we can close this quickly.

Attachments: nexus_outage_timeline.csv, redwood_edge_bgp_dump_20270411.txt, redwood_sso_logs_20270411.zip

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Nexus SRE Team <sre@nexuscloud.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@nexuscloud.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: exclude downstream peering outage from uptime calculation

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the details and the artifacts — we've begun an internal investigation. A few clarifying points from Nexus SRE:

- Nexus acknowledges an emergency config rollback in the peering cluster in US-W but we need to verify whether the customer-facing impact meets our third-party exclusion criteria. Our policy requires confirmation that the root cause was strictly within our peering fabric and that there were no simultaneous degradations in services we operate (control plane/BGP inject errors originating from Redwood are excluded).
- From preliminary checks, some traffic did failover but a segment continued to receive routes through the affected nodes for ~30 minutes due to stale BGP next-hops. That created elevated latency but limited 5xx amplification.

To assess exclusion we need the following from Redwood: 
1) Packet captures (PCAP) for a sample of affected flows during the window (captures should show TTL/BGP AS path info).
2) A precise list of IP prefixes and edge-hostnames that saw the degraded path (your BGP dump helps; a mapping to prefixes would speed review).
3) Clarify whether any Redwood-managed origin services (e.g., our mutual TLS handshakes) saw increases in retries — if so, that bears on shared responsibility.

If you can provide the above by EOD tomorrow (Mon 2027-04-12), Nexus will treat this as a formal exclusion request and expedite the review. Otherwise we will open a contested incident and begin normal SLA adjudication.

Regards,
Jordan Lee
Nexus Cloud SRE
ops@nexuscloud.com

Appreciate quick turnaround.
— Lauren

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: exclude downstream peering outage from uptime calculation

Lauren, Evelyn — quick technical summary and attached diag.

What I pulled:
- PCAP sample (sanitized) for three edge hosts that reported route changes; saved as redwood_edge_bgp_dump_20270411.txt (BGP update excerpts embedded) and a short PCAP subset we can share via secure transfer if Nexus prefers.
- We correlated request traces and saw ~14% of traffic from us-west used the affected peering ASN during the window. Of that 14%, approx 40% experienced p95 > 200ms; absolute 5xx spike was modest (~0.7% delta).
- Cache behavior: prefix-level KV caching meant many long-lived sessions continued unaffected; the impacted cohort was largely cold-start requests and a small set of enterprise customers with sticky routing.

Proposed language for Nexus: request a third-party exclusion for 15:03–16:37 UTC, and ask Nexus to accept exclusion for the full window. If Nexus accepts exclusion, Redwood will apply a pro-rata credit based on the impacted share (14% window-weighted) rather than full-window credit. Suggested credit calc attached in a one-line note: credit = SLA-window-credit * 0.14.

Attachments: peering_diag_screenshot.png, redwood_edge_bgp_dump_20270411.txt

Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: exclude downstream peering outage from uptime calculation

Jordan / Nexus SRE — attaching the numeric impact and a short rationale for the pro-rata credit approach.

Impact snapshot (us-west):
- Total requests during window: 9,120,000
- Requests routed via affected peer: 1,276,800 (14.0%)
- Affected requests with elevated p95: 511,000 (~5.6% of total; ~40% of the impacted cohort)
- 5xx delta during window: +0.7 percentage points (absolute)

Suggested remediation path:
1) If Nexus confirms the root cause is fully within their peering fabric and provides BGP announcements or a short writeup, Redwood requests Nexus mark 15:03–16:37 UTC as excluded for uptime calculations.
2) Redwood will accept a pro-rata credit using 14% as the impacted share; if Nexus prefers, we can instead apply a full-window exclusion provided Nexus issues an official incident exclusion note.

Attachments: nexus_impact_calc.xlsx (sent separately via secure share).

Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com

Cc: Nexus SRE Team <sre@nexuscloud.com>, ops@nexuscloud.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: exclude downstream peering outage from uptime calculation

Lauren / Evelyn / Marcus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. Nexus has completed its review.

Findings summary:
- Confirmed: an emergency rollback in our US-W peering cluster caused transient BGP next-hop inconsistencies. Root cause sits in our peering fabric.
- Evidence: Nexus has BGP update logs and we matched your BGP dump to our timeline; PCAP samples were helpful.

Outcome and next steps:
1) Nexus will mark 2027-04-11 15:03:00 UTC -> 16:37:00 UTC as a third-party exclusion for Redwood’s uptime tally. We will publish an exclusion note in the next 48 hours.
2) Nexus requests a signed acceptance of the exclusion terms (standard simple acknowledgement). We have prepared a short DocuSign form: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcdef — once signed, Nexus will finalize the exclusion in our SLA ledger.
3) Regarding credits: Nexus does not force a specific remediation credit model for partial degradations; we will accept Redwood’s pro-rata credit calculation provided the math is included in the signed acknowledgement.

Please sign the DocuSign and confirm the pro-rata factor (14%) so Nexus can close this item. If you prefer Nexus to issue a full-window exclusion instead of pro-rata credit, let us know and Nexus will record the full-window exclusion without a pro-rata offset.

Thanks — and apologies for the disruption. We’ll post the public incident note once the acknowledgement is complete.

Jordan Lee
Nexus Cloud SRE
jordan.lee@nexuscloud.com
